les: Party goedere is meer werd as ander
kaps_punt: Waardes van geselekteerde grondstowwe en vervaardigde goedere

items.bewering: 'n Woltrui het by 'n skaap begin en 'n brood het as koring in 'n saailand begin.
items.bron: Wool is shorn from sheep and processed into yarn: Maine State Museum, 'Wool Production In Depth' (mainestatemuseum.org) and Alberta wool fact sheet (alberta.wool.ca). Wheat is grown and harvested as a crop and then milled into flour for bread: UK Flour Millers, 'The milling process' (ukflourmillers.org/themillingprocess); primary-sector explainer, economicsonline.co.uk.

items.bewering: Wol en koring en water is dinge wat mense uit die natuur kry.
items.bron: Primary-sector definitions class farming (crops and livestock, including wool) as activities that take raw materials directly from nature (economicsonline.co.uk, 'Primary sector'); plants and animals are listed as renewable natural resources in geography references (sathee.iitk.ac.in, 'Geography: Natural resources'). Note for a person, not a fault: national-accounts frameworks (SEEA) treat cultivated crops and livestock as produced rather than natural assets, but the plain claim that wool and wheat come from nature holds and is standard at school-geography level.

items.bewering: 'n Ding uit die natuur wat mense gebruik noem ons 'n natuurlike hulpbron.
items.bron: Natural resources are 'materials or substances that occur in nature and can be used by humans' (designingbuildings.co.uk, 'Natural resource'); Freie Universitaet Berlin geography glossary, 'Natural resources' (geo.fu-berlin.de): natural substances and energy supplies that serve human needs.

items.bewering: Water is baie meer werd vir iemand wat ver geloop het as vir iemand by 'n kraan.
items.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: Paradox of value / marginal utility: the value of a unit of water depends on how scarce it is to the person (Wikipedia, 'Paradox of value'; economicsonline.co.uk, 'Exploring the paradox of value'). Mapping checked: whether 'walked far' is read as a thirsty walker or someone who must fetch water from far, water is scarcer or costlier to obtain for that person, so it is worth more to them; reasoned further, it leads a learner to scarcity raising value, which is exactly what the lesson teaches in 'Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is'. The comparison does not lead anywhere false.

items.bewering: Waarde is wat iets vir mense werd is. Dit is wat hulle bereid is om daarvoor te gee.
items.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: Economic value as the maximum a person is willing to give up to obtain something (ecosystemvaluation.org, 'Purpose of this website', section 1-01); Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'price': 'the value of something is how much other people would be willing to pay for it'.

items.bewering: 'n Prys is iets anders: dit is wat in geld daarvoor gevra word.
items.blok: Waarde en prys is nie dieselfde nie
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'price' (oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com): the amount of money asked or paid for something; Merriam-Webster Learner's Dictionary, 'price' (learnersdictionary.com): how much money is asked for goods. That price and value differ (market price is not the buyer's full valuation) is supported by ecosystemvaluation.org section 1-01.

items.bewering: Die wol in 'n woltrui is dieselfde wol wat op die skaap gegroei het.
items.bron: Wool processing (scouring, carding, spinning) cleans, sorts, aligns and twists the shorn fibres; it removes grease, dirt and short fibres but does not replace the fibre (Maine State Museum, 'Wool Production In Depth'; Alberta wool fact sheet on processing). The fibre in the garment is the shorn fibre.

items.bewering: Hulle het die skaap geskeer, die wol gewas en gespin en toe 'n trui gestrik.
items.bron: Sequence shearing -> scouring (washing) -> carding -> spinning -> knitting/weaving: Maine State Museum, 'Wool Production In Depth'; onlineclothingstudy.com, 'Processing of wool fibre'. Carding and sorting are omitted from the lesson's list, but the steps named are real and in the correct order, and the sentence does not claim to be complete.

items.bewering: Jy kan daardie werk nie in die trui sien nie.
items.bron: Read against the sentence before it, 'daardie werk' is the shearing, washing and spinning, and the point is that labour adds no visible substance: the processing sources (Maine State Museum; Alberta wool fact sheet) show the steps clean, align and twist the same fibre. The knitted stitches are visible, but they are the product of the work, not the work, so the sentence is defensible. This is a framing statement rather than a hard fact and is recorded so it is seen to have been looked at.

items.bewering: Die werk het van die wol iets gemaak wat mense wil dra. Daarom is die trui meer werd as die wol.
items.bron: Value added: the value a production process adds to the raw materials used (UNCTAD SDG Pulse glossary, 'Manufacturing value added', sdgpulse.unctad.org; accountingtools.com, 'Value added'). The wording ties the higher value to making something people want, which is consistent with the subjective-value statement in 'Waarde sit nie vas nie'.

items.bewering: 'n Meule maal die koring tot meel en 'n bakker bak die brode.
items.bron: UK Flour Millers / nabim, 'The milling process' (ukflourmillers.org/themillingprocess): wheat is broken and reduced on rollers to flour; Flour Info NZ, 'Flour milling process'; opentextbc.ca 'Understanding Ingredients for the Canadian Baker', ch. 'Milling of wheat'. A modern mill is a roller mill rather than millstones, but 'maal' covers both.

items.bewering: Die brode is meer werd as die koring waarmee begin is.
items.bron: GroundUp, 'What's up with the price of bread?' (groundup.org.za/article/whats-price-bread_2800): NAMC manager Christo Joubert says wheat is less than one-fifth of the total cost of bread, with milling, baking and transport making up the bulk. Grain SA, SA Grain March 2014: the wheat producer's share of a 700 g white loaf was 13-18% over 2008-2013 (about 588 g of wheat per 700 g loaf); Mail & Guardian, 12 April 2016: about 20%.

items.bewering: 'n Vervaardigde goed is meestal meer werd as die grondstof waaruit dit gemaak is.
items.bron: Value added is the difference between output value and input value; manufacturing normally produces goods worth more than their raw inputs (UNCTAD SDG Pulse, 'Manufacturing value added'; IDB Conexion INTAL, 'De los commodities al valor agregado', 29 Jan 2016). 'Meestal' correctly allows for exceptions (loss-making production).

items.bewering: Die werk en die kundigheid van mense het van die koring iets gemaak wat mense meer wil he.
items.bron: Same value-added sources as above; GroundUp/NAMC: milling and baking make up the bulk of the cost of a loaf, i.e. the human work and skill between grain and bread.

items.bewering: Dieselfde gebeur met koring en brood.
items.bron: Comparison mapping checked: the parallel drawn is that labour turns a raw material into something people want more, raising its value, which holds for both wool->jumper and wheat->bread (value-added sources above). It does not carry over the wool block's 'same material' claim to bread, which would be false (milling and baking change the grain), and the lesson does not make that claim.

items.bewering: Is daar min van 'n hulpbron en wil baie mense dit he, dan styg sy waarde. Is daar meer as genoeg daarvan, dan daal sy waarde.
items.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
items.bron: Law of supply and demand: shortage with demand pushes prices up, surplus pushes them down (LibreTexts, 'Introduction to Business (Lumen)', 7.16 Surpluses and Shortages, biz.libretexts.org; Kendall Hunt, Cipcic Macroeconomics 3e, Topic Two).

items.bewering: Werk laat waarde ook styg wanneer dit 'n grondstof verander in iets wat mense meer wil he.
items.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
items.bron: Value added (UNCTAD SDG Pulse; accountingtools.com). The condition 'wanneer ... iets wat mense meer wil he' keeps the claim within mainstream economics: labour raises value by producing something more wanted, not merely by being spent.

items.bewering: 'n Hulpbron wat ver moes kom is hier meer werd as waar dit uitgehaal is.
items.blok: Waarom party hulpbronne meer werd is
items.bron: Transport costs add to the delivered price with distance from the source (USDA-linked study of fresh produce wholesale prices, ageconsearch.umn.edu record 103696; Limao and Venables on transport costs rising with distance, CEPR DP2305). South African example: fuel costs more inland than at the coastal refineries and import terminals because of transport from the coast (Automobile Association, 'Petrol price breakdown', aa.co.za; Pretoria News / Business Report explainer, 3 October 2024).

items.bewering: Dieselfde hulpbron kan in die een jaar meer werd wees as in die ander. Was 'n oes swak, dan is daar minder koring en die waarde styg.
items.bron: Russia's 2010 drought cut its wheat crop and wheat prices rose to their highest since 2008 (NPR, 5 August 2010; PBS NewsHour, August 2010). South Africa: the 2015/16 drought cut the maize harvest from 14.25 to about 9.94 million tons and white maize reached record prices (Fin24, 30 December 2015 and 5 January 2016). Note for a person, not a fault: because South Africa imports about half its wheat and the local price sits near import parity, a poor South African wheat harvest alone moves the local price less than a poor world harvest does. The lesson states the general rule without a South African setting, so it holds as written.

items.bewering: Waarde is iets wat mense aan 'n hulpbron gee en nie iets wat in die ding sit nie.
items.bron: Subjective theory of value: the value of a good is not determined by any inherent property of the good; accepted by most mainstream schools of economics since Jevons, Menger and Walras (Wikipedia, 'Subjective theory of value'; Mises Institute, 'An Introduction to Austrian Economics', ch. 4). The older labour theory of value (classical economists, Marx) held otherwise; the lesson states the current mainstream view and stays consistent with it throughout, including in the labour blocks.

items.bewering: natuurlike hulpbron: Iets uit die natuur wat mense gebruik, soos water, hout of steenkool.
items.bron: designingbuildings.co.uk, 'Natural resource'; FU Berlin geography glossary, 'Natural resources' (soil, water, coal, gas); wordsmyth.net, 'natural resource' (fresh water, soil, coal, forests). All three examples are standard natural resources.

items.bewering: waarde: Wat iets vir mense werd is en wat hulle daarvoor wil gee.
items.bron: Willingness-to-pay definition of economic value (ecosystemvaluation.org section 1-01); Oxford Learner's Dictionaries usage note distinguishing value (what people would be willing to pay) from price. Consistent with the study block's definition, so the entry reads correctly on its own.

opsomming: All 22 claims hold against sources, so this goes to approval. There are no superlatives in the lesson, and both comparisons (water for someone who walked far, and 'the same happens with wheat and bread') were checked for where they lead and do not lead anywhere false. Two nuances are noted but are not faults: wheat and wool count as natural resources in school geography but not in national-accounts terms, and a poor South African wheat harvest alone moves the local price less than a poor world harvest, because about half of South Africa's wheat is imported.
